title: First text encoder: additive next-token fit-and-report on wikitext-103 (the M131 machinery)
question: Does the M131 additive next-token construction build a frozen text arm on wikitext-103 character tokens, with the window dial behaving as measured on the DSL (perplexity falls, footprint grows, more memory does not hurt)?

corpus.note: test is held-out and read-only; nothing is fitted on it

anchors.g1: window-1 test perplexity equals the independent closed-form bigram computation to <= 1e-9

gate.more_memory_hurts: fired if test_ppl(window=max) > test_ppl(window=1) * 1.10 (uniform variant; a fired switch is a reported negative per N90.5)

comparison_arm.registered: longest-match backoff read (continuations primitive, add-alpha at the matched order, uniform floor for novel contexts), same window ladder — registered before the sealed run (18 Aug 2026)
comparison_arm.verdict_clause: A0 selects NO arm from test numbers; the ladder + fired gate answer the cell, and cells A/D pin their arm in A's own registration using a validation slice

role: this encoder is the frozen text arm reused by cells A (text->text transfer) and D (license-clean Wikipedia fit-and-report)
